findings.title: Regex character class too broad due to '-' being treated as range operator
findings.body: The regex `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` contains the character class `[a-zA-Z-_]`. In Java regex, the dash '-' that is not at the start or end of the class and not escaped is interpreted as a range operator. With the previous 'A-Z' range ending at 'Z' (0x5A), the '-_' is parsed as a range from 'Z' (0x5A) to '_' (0x5F), which silently adds '[', '\', ']', '^', and '_' to the matched character set. The author clearly intended `[a-zA-Z_]` (or `[a-zA-Z_-]` with '-' placed last so it is a literal). For typical locale codes (letters + underscore) this happens to work, but the regex is incorrect and could match unintended characters in path components containing '[', '\', etc. Fix by writing `[a-zA-Z_-]` (dash at the end of the class, making it literal) or `[a-zA-Z_]`.

findings.title: Stale Matcher iterates over the original string while value is mutated
findings.body: In `santizeAnchors`, `Matcher matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)` is created once against the original `value`, but `value` is reassigned inside the loop via `value = value.replaceFirst(...)`. Java's Matcher retains a reference to the original CharSequence and continues iterating from where it left off in that original buffer even after `value` now points to a newly-allocated string. Consequence: the matcher can 'find' anchors that have already been removed from the current `value`, and conversely can miss anchors that only exist in the modified string. With repeated anchors (e.g. translation `a b` vs English `x`), iteration will process the second `` against an exhausted EnglishMatcher and report "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string", producing a false-positive. The fix is to either (a) re-create `matcher = ANCHOR_PATTERN.matcher(value)` after each `replaceFirst`, or (b) iterate via `Matcher.results()` and build a new string, or (c) tokenize the string with the matcher and rebuild.

findings.title: replaceFirst only removes the first occurrence of a repeated anchor
findings.body: `value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "")` only replaces the FIRST match in `value`, not all matches. If a translation legitimately reuses the same anchor tag more than once and the English source only has one occurrence, only the first occurrence is stripped; the remaining occurrences are then passed to the OWASP sanitizer, which (with `POLICY_SOME_HTML` not allowing `<a>`) will escape them and produce a spurious "Illegal HTML" error. Combined with the stale-Matcher issue above, the second `<a href="X">` is also reported as "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string". Use `replaceAll`, or iterate via the matcher and reconstruct the string, to handle repeated anchors correctly.

findings.title: Comment mischaracterises '<1>' as a "numeric tag"
findings.body: The comment states the sanitizer escapes 'numeric tags like `<1>`'. There is no concept of a numeric tag in HTML or in the OWASP sanitizer; the sanitizer simply treats the literal text `<1>` as an invalid HTML tag (because tag names must start with a letter per the policy) and escapes the '<' and '>' characters. `<1>` here is an i18next / React-Intl style indexed placeholder, not a numeric tag. The wording will mislead future maintainers about what the sanitizer is doing and why `<1>` survives the round-trip via `unescapeHtml4`.

findings.title: Breaking change to i18next escape syntax in JS-side resource bundle
findings.body: The value of `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The double-brace form `{{0}}` / `{{1}}` / `{{2}}` is i18next's escape syntax for producing literal `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` text, which is what account-ui uses. After this change, i18next will interpret `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and the `{2,choice,...}` clause as placeholders / interpolation tokens. i18next does not implement Java MessageFormat choice format, and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` is not valid i18next interpolation syntax, so the message will either fail to interpolate or be displayed verbatim with broken `{...}` text instead of the localized error. The previous value (`value(s)`) was a deliberate, working i18next-compatible rendering of the message; this PR regresses that. The new format belongs only on the Java side (e.g. `themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/messages/messages_en.properties`), where it does belong.

findings.title: Same i18next breaking change in admin-ui resource bundle
findings.body: Same regression as in the account-ui bundle: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to Java MessageFormat syntax (`{0}`, `{1}`, `{2,choice,...}`). The admin-ui is also a React/i18next app, so the change replaces working placeholder-escaping with placeholders that i18next will try to interpolate, and embeds a Java MessageFormat choice clause (`{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`) that i18next does not understand. Result at runtime: malformed interpolation and/or broken/untranslated text shown to the admin user.

findings.title: No positive test that valid HTML in a translation is accepted
findings.body: The four new tests only assert that illegal HTML is detected (`verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected`, `verifyNoHtmlAllowed`, `verifyNoChangedAnchors`) and that duplicates are detected. There is no positive test that exercises the happy path of `verifySafeHtml`: e.g. an English value containing `bar` and a translation containing `bar` (or `bar`) that should NOT be reported. Without it, a regression in the sanitizer flow (e.g. always escaping ``) would not be caught by the test suite. Add a test resource pair (`allowedHtml_en.properties` + `allowedHtml_de.properties`) with matching allowed tags and assert that the message list does not contain "Illegal HTML".

findings.title: No test for the `{2,choice,...}` normalization of `error-invalid-multivalued-size`
findings.body: `normalizeValue` strips `{N,choice,...}` clauses for `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit.*` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size` specifically. This special case is central to the PR because that key was just rewritten across every bundle to use this Java MessageFormat choice syntax. There is no test fixture nor assertion that (a) a translation whose choice clause differs from the English (e.g. different `1#value|1<values` text) is still accepted, and (b) a translation with literal `<` outside a choice clause is rejected. The whole point of this PR is to make `error-invalid-multivalued-size` valid, but the only protection against regressing it is the production code itself, with no regression test in `VerifyMessagePropertiesTest`.

findings.title: File is read and parsed twice per verification
findings.body: `verify()` reads the file with `Files.readString(file.toPath())` for duplicate-key detection, and then `verifySafeHtml()` opens another `FileInputStream` and parses the same file as `PropertyResourceBundle`. The two reads produce no consistency guarantee (a file could change between reads) and double the I/O. Either parse once into a `PropertyResourceBundle` and reuse it for both checks, or read the bytes once and wrap them in two parsers. Not a correctness bug, but the verifier runs over hundreds of message bundles during a theme build, so the duplication is non-trivial.

findings.title: Trailing newline stripped from `error-invalid-multivalued-size`
findings.body: The unified diff shows the file ends with `\ No newline at end of file` after this change (the `-` line also had `\ No newline at end of file`). Many editors, linters, and POSIX text tools require files to end with a newline, and several Keycloak bundles historically did so. The fact that the previous version ended without a newline was already a minor smell, but the change also touches a line at the end of the file without restoring the newline. This will show up as a noisy diff in future PRs and may violate any project policy on POSIX file endings.
